lines: {"node_id": "NRS_484B_400_2b", "law_refs": ["NRS-484B-400-2b"], "subject": {"binder": "v", "class_elements": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]}, "segmentation": [{"id": "s1", "text": "If the driver of a vehicle", "role": "subject"}, {"id": "s2", "text": "intends to turn", "role": "condition"}, {"id": "s3", "text": "at an intersection and:", "role": "condition"}, {"id": "s4", "text": "Both intersecting highways are two-directional:", "role": "condition"}, {"id": "s5", "text": "After entering the intersection,", "role": "condition"}, {"id": "s6", "text": "the left turn", "role": "condition"}, {"id": "s7", "text": "must be made so as to leave the intersection to the right of the centerline of the highway being entered.", "role": "obligation"}], "elements": [{"span": "s1", "atoms": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"], "derived": [], "justification": "'vehicle' is a legal aggregate and the definitions table admits DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle for this law; ru.aggregate carries 'membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id', so the words are claimed as the one atom with that id. Exclusions: st.median_or_divider is read for the physical barrier its contract denotes and not for a legal designation of a highway, which would be an assumption; st.lane_direction is local to its carrier, which is why it is read on the carriers of each intersecting way and not at a point; st.roadway is not a stand-in for the sidewalk, which is not read."}, {"span": "s5", "atoms": ["rel.occupies", "st.intersection"], "derived": ["drv.motion.region_entry"], "justification": "drv.motion.region_entry is 'the road user's footprint comes to overlap a structure region at the observation: it overlaps the region at the observation and did not overlap it at the observation before ... the event of that coming to overlap', which is 'entering the intersection'; the region formal is bound to the intersection s3 singles out, so the entry is into that junction and not into any region of its kind. rel.occupies anchors the vehicle on the region and st.intersection is the kind the region quantifier names. At the observation at which its footprint ceases to overlap the junction it is on the far side of the entered way's centre line, the centre line lying to its right.", "masked": []}, {"name": "permit", "expected": "compliant", "narrative": "The same two two-directional ways, the same declared intention, the same entry and left turn; at the observation at which the subject's footprint ceases to overlap the junction the centre line of the way it then occupies lies to its left by more than the lateral-offset resolution. lines: {"node_id": "NRS_484B_400_2b", "law_refs": ["NRS-484B-400-2b"], "subject": {"binder": "v", "class_elements": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]}, "segmentation": [{"id": "s1", "text": "If the driver of a vehicle", "role": "subject"}, {"id": "s2", "text": "intends to turn", "role": "condition"}, {"id": "s3", "text": "at an intersection and:", "role": "condition"}, {"id": "s4", "text": "Both intersecting highways are two-directional:", "role": "condition"}, {"id": "s5", "text": "After entering the intersection,", "role": "condition"}, {"id": "s6", "text": "the left turn", "role": "condition"}, {"id": "s7", "text": "must be made so as to leave the intersection to the right of the centerline of the highway being entered.", "role": "obligation"}], "elements": [{"span": "s1", "atoms": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"], "derived": [], "justification": "'vehicle' is a legal aggregate and the definitions table admits DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle for this law; ru.aggregate carries 'membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id', so the words are claimed as the one atom with that id. Exclusions: not a stand-in for a named road-user class, since no class atom is used and the aggregate stays one atom; not a stand-in for a relational role such as who drives or controls a vehicle, so 'the driver' is not carried by the aggregate but read through the vehicle's controlled motion (narrowing on this span)."}, {"span": "s3", "atoms": ["rel.occupies", "st.intersection", "st.lane_enters", "st.travel_region"], "derived": [], "justification": "Reuse of the mapping index for these same words in NRS_484B_400_2a. st.intersection is 'the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges', the junction the words name; rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region', anchors the vehicle to the carrier it is on, and st.lane_enters gives 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end', so the intersection the words single out is the one the carrier the vehicle occupies enters; st.travel_region, 'the union of the kinds a device can govern: a lane and the kinds that refine it ... a roadway ... or an intersection', is the kind the carrier quantifier ranges over. Exclusions: st.intersection is not a stand-in for a crosswalk or a stop line, neither of which is read; st.lane_enters is not a stand-in for lane connectivity or for the subject's presence in the intersection, which rel.occupies carries; st.travel_region is not a stand-in for the extent of a highway, read by its own atom on s4."}, {"span": "s4", "atoms": ["rel.occupies", "st.highway", "st.intersection", "st.lane_direction", "st.lane_enters", "st.median_or_divider", "st.on_way", "st.roadway", "st.travel_region"], "derived": [], "justification": "Reuse of the mapping index for these same words in NRS_484B_400_2a. DEF-NRS-484B-073 defines a two-directional highway as 'an undivided highway upon which vehicles are allowed to proceed in opposite directions': st.median_or_divider, 'physical barrier or dividing section between roadways', carries 'undivided' by the absence of such a region on the way, and st.lane_direction, 'direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in ... a roadway, one-way roadway or shoulder', carries 'proceed in opposite directions' by two carriers of the same way carrying opposed designated directions. The two ways are reached through the junction: st.lane_enters names the carriers whose entrance end is that intersection, st.travel_region is the kind they are quantified by, st.roadway 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic' is the kind whose directions are designated, st.on_way 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on' and st.highway 'the entire public way between its boundary lines' give the highway each carrier lies on, st.intersection the junction itself, and rel.occupies anchors the subject. Exclusions: st.median_or_divider is read for the physical barrier its contract denotes and not for a legal designation of a highway, which would be an assumption; st.lane_direction is local to its carrier, which is why it is read on the carriers of each intersecting way and not at a point; st.roadway is not a stand-in for the sidewalk, which is not read."}, {"span": "s5", "atoms": ["rel.occupies", "st.intersection"], "derived": ["drv.motion.region_entry"], "justification": "drv.motion.region_entry is 'the road user's footprint comes to overlap a structure region at the observation: it overlaps the region at the observation and did not overlap it at the observation before ... the event of that coming to overlap', which is 'entering the intersection'; the region formal is bound to the intersection s3 singles out, so the entry is into that junction and not into any region of its kind. rel.occupies anchors the vehicle on the region and st.intersection is the kind the region quantifier names. The mapping index maps 'prior to entering an intersection' to the same carriers. Exclusions: the concept is not a stand-in for lying within the region afterwards, which rel.occupies carries on its own, nor for the carrier the road user came through."}, {"span": "s6", "atoms": [], "derived": ["drv.motion.left_turn"], "justification": "drv.motion.left_turn is 'the road user has turned to the left: counting from the onset of the turning ... the heading change accumulated since that onset reaches at least the turn angle ... to the left', which is 'the left turn' the words name, the manoeuvre whose manner the obligation governs. Exclusions: the concept is not a stand-in for a signal or a declared intention (the intention of s2 is carried by int.turn), not for a steering input, not for the curvature of the road, not for a lane change, and not for a reversal of the direction of travel, which is a larger angle with its own concept."}, {"span": "s7", "atoms": ["prim.region_lateral_offset", "rel.occupies", "st.centre_line", "st.highway", "st.intersection", "st.on_way"], "derived": ["drv.motion.region_exit"], "justification": "'leave the intersection' is drv.motion.region_exit, 'the road user's footprint ceases to overlap a structure region at the observation: it does not overlap the region at the observation and did overlap it at the observation before ... the event of that ceasing to overlap', with its region formal bound to the intersection s3 singles out, so the departure is from that junction; rel.occupies anchors the vehicle and st.intersection is the kind that region quantifier names. 'the centerline of the highway being entered' is a st.centre_line region, 'the marking, or the geometric centre, dividing the two directions of a two-way roadway', tied to the way by st.on_way, 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on', on the st.highway region, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines', that the vehicle occupies at that observation (rel.occupies). 'to the right of' is prim.region_lateral_offset, 'the signed lateral offset (m, left positive) of a structure region from a road user ... the component, perpendicular to the road user's heading, of the vector from its reference point to the point of the region's boundary nearest that reference point': the centre line lies to the vehicle's left, so the vehicle lies to its right. Exclusions: prim.region_lateral_offset 'does not establish that the road user is on the carrier', which rel.occupies does; st.centre_line is the dividing marking or geometric centre and no lane or lane adjacency stands in for it; st.highway is not a stand-in for the roadway, and the words name the highway being entered."}], "operationalizations": [], "assumptions": [], "intentions": [{"span": "s2", "id": "int.turn", "meaning": "the source's current plan for the road user is that it turn, to either hand, at the region named as the declaration's target"}], "compositions": [], "residues": [], "binders": [], "applicability": "The subject vehicle v occupies a carrier whose entrance end is an intersection i (st.lane_enters, the carrier quantified over st.travel_region, rel.occupies); the source's current declaration for v at i is int.turn; both highways that meet at i are two-directional, each way carrying no median or dividing section (st.median_or_divider absent on it) and carriers of its roadway carrying opposed designated directions (st.lane_direction), the ways reached by st.on_way and st.highway from the carriers that enter i; v has entered i (drv.motion.region_entry on i at the judged observation or at an earlier one); and v has made a left turn (drv.motion.left_turn, with p.turn_onset_yaw_rate, p.left_turn_angle and the step bound p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph).", "obligation": "At the observation at which v leaves i (drv.motion.region_exit on the intersection i the applicability binds), v lies to the right of the centre line of the highway it then occupies: for the st.highway region h with rel.occupies(v, h) at that observation there is a st.centre_line region c with st.on_way(c, h) whose signed lateral offset from v, prim.region_lateral_offset (left positive), is at least p.lateral_offset_resolution. Where no such centre line is observed on that way the obligation is unknown, not met.", "params": ["p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph", "p.turn_onset_yaw_rate", "p.left_turn_angle", "p.lateral_offset_resolution"], "narrowings": [{"span": "s1", "why": "'the driver of a vehicle' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the ontology's section on what is not an atom directs that 'drives', 'operates' and 'the driver' are read through the vehicle's controlled motion, a vehicle moving on the road is taken to be driven, and the duty binds that vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.", "kind": "observable_reading", "category": "agency"}, {"span": "s7", "why": "'the highway being entered' is read as the st.highway region the vehicle occupies at the observation at which it leaves the intersection, and 'the centerline' of it as a centre-line region lying on that way (st.on_way). The words leave open which way is meant; this is the way the vehicle is on once it is clear of the junction, the junction itself lying on every way that meets there.", "kind": "reading"}, {"span": "s7", "why": "'to the right of the centerline' is read as the centre line's signed lateral offset from the vehicle standing at or above p.lateral_offset_resolution on the left-positive side, the magnitude below which the side a region lies on is not distinguishable at the source's resolution; the side is read across the vehicle's own heading, which at the departure from the junction lies along the way entered.", "kind": "reading"}], "scenarios": [{"name": "forbid", "expected": "violated", "narrative": "Two undivided ways, each with carriers of opposed designated directions, cross; the trace declares the subject's intention to turn at that junction; the subject enters the junction and its accumulated heading change to the left passes the turn angle, so a left turn is made. At the observation at which its footprint ceases to overlap the junction it is on the far side of the entered way's centre line, the centre line lying to its right.", "masked": []}, {"name": "permit", "expected": "compliant", "narrative": "The same two two-directional ways, the same declared intention, the same entry and left turn; at the observation at which the subject's footprint ceases to overlap the junction the centre line of the way it then occupies lies to its left by more than the lateral-offset resolution. No other road user is present in the scene.", "masked": []}, {"name": "idle", "expected": "not_applicable", "narrative": "The subject runs straight through the same junction: the trace declares no intention to turn for it at that junction and its accumulated heading change never reaches the turn angle, so no left turn is made.", "masked": []}, {"name": "blind", "expected": "unknown", "narrative": "Every other condition holds -- two two-directional ways, the declared intention, the entry, and a departure from the junction on the left of the entered way's centre line -- but the source supplies no rate of change of heading for the subject, so whether it has turned to the left cannot be told.", "masked": ["kin.yaw_rate"]}, {"name": "branch_1", "expected": "not_applicable", "narrative": "The way being entered carries a median dividing its two directions, so the intersecting ways are not both two-directional; the subject, with a declared intention to turn, enters the junction, turns left and leaves it on the left of that way's centre line.", "masked": []}], "literals": [], "param_proposals": [], "gaps": []}

{"node_id": "NRS_484B_407", "law_refs": ["NRS-484B-407"], "subject": {"binder": "v", "class_elements": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]}, "segmentation": [{"id": "s1", "text": "A vehicle", "role": "subject"}, {"id": "s2", "text": "shall not be turned so as to proceed in the opposite direction", "role": "obligation"}, {"id": "s3", "text": "upon any curve,", "role": "condition"}, {"id": "s4", "text": "or upon the approach to or near the crest of a grade,", "role": "condition"}, {"id": "s5", "text": "where such vehicle cannot be seen by the driver of any other vehicle approaching from either direction within 500 feet.", "role": "condition"}], "elements": [{"span": "s1", "atoms": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"], "derived": [], "justification": "'vehicle' is a legal aggregate and the definitions table admits DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle for this law; ru.aggregate carries 'membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id'. Exclusions: not a stand-in for a named road-user class, no class atom being used; not a stand-in for a relational role, the words naming the vehicle itself and not its driver."}, {"span": "s2", "atoms": [], "derived": ["drv.motion.u_turn"], "justification": "drv.motion.u_turn is 'the road user's direction of travel upon a way has reversed ... the magnitude of the heading change accumulated since that onset reaches at least the reversal angle ... while the road user's footprint overlaps a way', and its contract carries the very words of this obligation: 'the turning of a vehicle upon a highway so as to proceed in the opposite direction', 'whether accomplished by one continuous movement or not', so halts and rearward movements between the onset and the reversal do not end the manoeuvre. Exclusions: it is not a stand-in for a turn through a smaller angle, which has its own concept, nor for travel against a designated direction of travel, nor for a reversing movement, nor for a signal or a declared intention."}, {"span": "s3", "atoms": ["rel.occupies", "st.curvature", "st.roadway"], "derived": [], "justification": "st.curvature is 'horizontal curvature of the roadway at a point, as a magnitude (1/m, never negative): a bend to either hand has the same value', which is 'any curve'; the words name the feature and no size of it, so it is carried by the magnitude standing clear of zero, at or above p.curvature_resolution, a parameter that names the source's resolution only and no measure of how sharp a bend must be. rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region', anchors the vehicle on the region whose curvature is read, and st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic', is the kind that region quantifier names, the curvature being the roadway's. Exclusions: st.curvature is not the crest of a grade, read on s4 by its own atom, and not the sight distance the bend restricts, read on s5; st.roadway is not a stand-in for the sidewalk, which is not read."}, {"span": "s4", "atoms": ["rel.occupies", "st.crest", "st.region_geometry", "st.roadway"], "derived": [], "justification": "st.crest is 'the place on a roadway's longitudinal profile where the slope changes from rising to falling in the direction of travel, carried as a region with a reference point and a boundary, so the ground distance from a road user to it is read through st.region_geometry', which is 'the crest of a grade'; 'the approach to or near' it is that ground distance, st.region_geometry giving 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it', at most p.crest_approach_distance. rel.occupies anchors the vehicle on the roadway and st.roadway is the kind the region quantifier names for the way the profile belongs to. Exclusions: st.crest is expressly 'not a stand-in for the slope at a point (st.grade)', which is why no grade atom is read, nor for 'the view a crest restricts (st.sight_distance)', read on s5 by its own atom, nor for 'a horizontal bend (st.curvature)', read on s3; st.region_geometry is not a stand-in for occupancy, which rel.occupies carries."}, {"span": "s5", "atoms": ["rel.occupies", "st.roadway", "st.sight_distance"], "derived": [], "justification": "st.sight_distance is 'the distance along the road within which a vehicle at a point and another vehicle on the road could see each other, from the eye of either driver to the body of the other vehicle at the height convention the source declares: both the view of approaching traffic from that point and its being seen by drivers approaching it, whether or not any road user is there'. The words 'such vehicle cannot be seen by the driver of any other vehicle approaching from either direction within 500 feet' are exactly that quantity at the vehicle's place falling short of the stated 500 feet, and the contract's 'whether or not any road user is there' is why the duty binds the subject with no other vehicle in the scene. rel.occupies anchors the vehicle on the road whose sight distance is read and st.roadway is the kind that region quantifier names. Exclusions: it is 'not a stand-in for whether an actual road user saw, or could see, another at an observation (rel.visible)', and the words ask of any approaching driver, not of one present; not for 'the clarity of the air (env.visibility)'; and not st.sight_along_way, whose contract is the view from a road user's own eye along a way, while the words ask whether the vehicle can be seen at its place."}], "operationalizations": [], "assumptions": [], "intentions": [], "compositions": [], "residues": [], "binders": [], "applicability": "The subject vehicle v occupies a roadway, and at one and the same moment while the reversal is under way (the words join the place and the sight condition by 'where'): either the horizontal curvature of the roadway at v's place stands at or above p.curvature_resolution, or the ground distance from v's body to a st.crest region on the roadway is at most p.crest_approach_distance; and the sight distance of v's place (st.sight_distance) falls short of 500 feet.", "obligation": "v does not turn upon the way so as to proceed in the opposite direction: the rule is violated where drv.motion.u_turn is recognized for v (with p.turn_onset_yaw_rate, p.u_turn_reversal_angle and the step bound p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph) and the applicability's conditions held together at a moment of that act; it is complied with where the conditions so held and no such act is recognized.", "params": ["p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph", "p.turn_onset_yaw_rate", "p.u_turn_reversal_angle", "p.curvature_resolution", "p.crest_approach_distance"], "narrowings": [{"span": "s4", "why": "'the approach to or near the crest of a grade' is read as one ground distance from the vehicle's body to the crest region, at most p.crest_approach_distance, without distinguishing the upstream side from the downstream one: the words' own 'or near the crest' covers the vicinity on either hand, and the atom carries the crest as a region and the distance to it, not the side.", "kind": "reading"}, {"span": "s5", "why": "'from either direction' is read through the sight distance of the vehicle's place, which the atom's contract defines as covering both the view of approaching traffic from that point and its being seen by drivers approaching it; the atom carries one value for the place, so the worse of the two directions is not distinguished from the better.", "kind": "reading"}, {"span": "s5", "why": "'cannot be seen by the driver of any other vehicle' is read as what could be seen at the place, whether or not any road user is there, as the atom's contract states and as the ontology directs for a duty to be seen: no perception of an actual driver is read.", "kind": "observable_reading", "category": "perception"}], "occasion": {"act": "drv.motion.u_turn", "boundary": "event", "onset": {"words": "counting from the onset of the manoeuvre -- the observation at which the magnitude of its rate of change of heading first rose above the onset yaw rate", "atoms": ["kin.yaw_rate"], "derived": [], "justification": "The concept's contract fixes the act's observed beginning at that observation, and the only quantity it reads there is kin.yaw_rate, 'rate of change of heading, positive when the heading turns to the left (counter-clockwise)'. Exclusion: kin.yaw_rate is 'not a stand-in for road curvature', which this node reads on s3 by its own atom for the place, not for the manoeuvre."}, "recognition": "the observation at which the magnitude of the heading change accumulated since that onset first reaches the reversal angle, which is where the concept rises; the later observations at which the accumulated change still holds that angle are not the act again.", "under_way": {"words": "the magnitude of the road user's rate of change of heading has stood above the onset yaw rate since the onset and the accumulated heading change has not yet reached the reversal angle", "atoms": ["kin.yaw_rate"], "derived": [], "justification": "An observation inside the act is told from one before it began by the road user's own motion: its rate of change of heading, the quantity the concept's onset and accumulation read. No place or region tells them apart, since the vehicle occupies the same bend, the same crest vicinity and the same place before the manoeuvre begins."}, "spans": {"s3": "some_moment", "s4": "some_moment", "s5": "some_moment"}}, "scenarios": [{"name": "forbid", "expected": "violated", "narrative": "The subject runs along a bend whose horizontal curvature stands well above the resolution, and the sight distance of its place falls short of the figure the text states. On that bend it swings through more than the reversal angle and proceeds back the way it came.", "masked": []}, {"name": "permit", "expected": "compliant", "narrative": "The same bend with the same short sight distance; the subject turns off into a side way, its accumulated heading change staying far below the reversal angle, and never proceeds in the opposite direction. No other road user is present in the scene.", "masked": []}, {"name": "idle", "expected": "not_applicable", "narrative": "On a straight and level stretch, no crest region within the approach distance and the place's sight distance well beyond the stated figure, the subject swings through more than the reversal angle and proceeds back the way it came.", "masked": []}, {"name": "blind", "expected": "unknown", "narrative": "The subject reverses its direction on a bend whose curvature is recorded, but the source declares no sight distance for the places along it, so whether the vehicle could be seen within the stated distance cannot be told.", "masked": ["st.sight_distance"]}, {"name": "occasion_s3", "expected": "violated", "narrative": "The subject begins the reversal on the bend and completes it where the alignment has run out straight: the curvature stands above the resolution at the onset and the first part of the manoeuvre only, and the sight distance at those same observations falls short of the stated figure.", "masked": []}, {"name": "occasion_s3_outside", "expected": "not_applicable", "narrative": "The subject runs along the bend, leaves it, and only then, on a straight stretch with no crest region within the approach distance, swings through more than the reversal angle; the curvature stands above the resolution only at observations before the onset, while the sight distance is short throughout.", "masked": []}, {"name": "occasion_s4", "expected": "violated", "narrative": "The subject begins the reversal with the crest region within the approach distance of its body and completes it farther down the grade, beyond that distance; the alignment is straight throughout and the sight distance at the observations near the crest falls short of the stated figure.", "masked": []}, {"name": "occasion_s4_outside", "expected": "not_applicable", "narrative": "The subject passes the crest, runs on until the crest region lies beyond the approach distance, and only then swings through more than the reversal angle on a straight stretch; the crest was within the approach distance only at observations before the onset, while the sight distance is short throughout.", "masked": []}, {"name": "occasion_s5", "expected": "violated", "narrative": "The subject reverses its direction on a bend whose curvature stands above the resolution at every observation of the manoeuvre, and the sight distance of its place falls short of the stated figure at the onset and the first part of the manoeuvre, rising above it before the reversal is complete.", "masked": []}, {"name": "occasion_s5_outside", "expected": "not_applicable", "narrative": "The subject runs on the bend through a stretch whose sight distance falls short of the stated figure, and begins and completes the reversal farther along the same bend, where the sight distance at its place exceeds the stated figure at every observation from the onset onwards.", "masked": []}], "literals": [{"span": "s5", "text": "500 feet", "value": 500, "unit": "ft"}], "param_proposals": [{"name": "p.curvature_resolution", "unit": "1/m", "value": 0.001, "convention": "Map-geometry resolution convention: the magnitude of horizontal curvature below which a surveyed road alignment is indistinguishable from a tangent at the resolution of the source, a radius of the order of a kilometre. It names the source's resolution only and sets no bound on how sharp a bend must be for the duty to bind.", "source": "highway alignment survey practice, in which curves of radius above about a kilometre are recorded as tangents in the road geometry of a map or simulator."}, {"name": "p.crest_approach_distance", "unit": "m", "value": 150.0, "convention": "Crest sight-distance convention: the distance from a crest within which the crest's vertical curve restricts the view of the road beyond it, taken as the length of the crest vertical curve of the design standard at open-road design speed; it bounds 'the approach to or near' the crest on either side.", "source": "AASHTO Green Book crest vertical curve lengths and stopping sight distance tables for open-road design speeds."}], "gaps": []}

{"node_id": "NRS_484B_413_2", "law_refs": ["NRS-484B-413-2"], "subject": {"binder": "v", "class_elements": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]}, "segmentation": [{"id": "s1", "text": "A signal of intention to turn right or left, or otherwise turn a vehicle from a direct course, shall be given continuously during not less than the last 100 feet traveled", "role": "obligation"}, {"id": "s2", "text": "in a business or residential district and not less than the last 300 feet traveled in any other area", "role": "condition"}, {"id": "s3", "text": "prior to changing the course of a vehicle.", "role": "condition"}, {"id": "s4", "text": "This rule shall be observed, regardless of the weather.", "role": "condition"}], "elements": [{"span": "s1", "atoms": ["kin.path_length", "kin.yaw_rate", "ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle", "sig.hand_signal", "sig.turn_indicator"], "derived": [], "justification": "sig.turn_indicator is 'the turn indicator state in {off, left, right}: neither indicator lit, or the left or the right one' and sig.hand_signal is 'a driver's or rider's arm signal; meaning in {no_signal, left, right, stop_or_slow, re_enter}'; together they carry 'a signal of intention to turn right or left', the ontology directing that a signal 'of intention' is the signal itself and not a declared intention. kin.path_length, 'distance travelled along the body's path since the start of the trace, monotone', is what the window 'the last 100 feet traveled' measures: a distance-travelled window reads it as a time window reads the clock. kin.yaw_rate, 'rate of change of heading, positive when the heading turns to the left', gives the hand of the course change, so that the signal required is the indication of that hand. ru.aggregate carries 'a vehicle' by the admitted id DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle. Exclusions: sig.turn_indicator is 'not a stand-in for the turn or lane change itself', which s3 carries by its concept; sig.hand_signal is not the rider's posture; kin.yaw_rate is 'not a stand-in for road curvature', no road geometry being read; kin.path_length is the subject's own travelled distance and not a position."}, {"span": "s3", "atoms": [], "derived": ["drv.motion.turning"], "justification": "drv.motion.turning is 'the road user's heading is changing at the observation: the magnitude of its heading change over the window behind the observation is at least the heading change tolerance ... a state the road user is in at each observation of a bending path, in either hand', which is 'changing the course of a vehicle', the law's own 'turn right or left, or otherwise turn ... from a direct course'. 'prior to' is read from the observation at which that change is first recognized, the rise of the concept, and the window of travelled path runs back from it. Exclusions: the concept is not a stand-in for a completed turn, a steering input, the curvature of the road, a lane change, or a signal or an intention, the signal being carried on s1 by its own atoms."}], "operationalizations": [], "assumptions": [{"span": "s2", "id": "asm.in_business_or_residential_district", "meaning": "the map or trace declares that the stretch of highway the road user occupies at the observation lies within a business district or a residential district"}], "intentions": [], "compositions": [], "residues": [{"span": "s4", "why": "The words add no observable condition and no restriction: the signal is owed over the same window, in the same terms, whether or not rain, snow, wet road, ice or any other weather is present, so the duty is the same whether or not these words hold. The rule reads no weather atom for them, and nothing of the obligation is dropped.", "scope": "none"}], "binders": [], "applicability": "The subject vehicle v changes its course: at the judged observation drv.motion.turning rises for v, its heading change over p.turn_recognition_window first reaching p.heading_change_noise_floor. The trace's declaration asm.in_business_or_residential_district selects the window; where the trace declares it neither true nor false the verdict is unknown.", "obligation": "Over the window of path travelled behind that observation -- 100 feet where asm.in_business_or_residential_district holds and 300 feet where it does not, the length selected by a condition on that declaration and measured as a distance-travelled window on kin.path_length -- v gave the signal of the hand of the course change at every observation of the window: sig.turn_indicator in the state of that hand, or sig.hand_signal with that hand's meaning. {"concept_id": "drv.motion.region_exit", "kind": "formula", "contract": "The road user's footprint ceases to overlap a structure region at the observation: it does not overlap the region at the observation and did overlap it at the observation before. The concept is the event of that ceasing to overlap, read at the observation at which the overlap has ended, and not the state of lying outside the region at the later observations. It states no direction of departure, no carrier the road user leaves through, no speed and no place outside the region. Not a stand-in for: lying outside the region, which the occupancy relation carries on its own; a later observation at which the road user is still outside; the carrier or the way the road user goes on to, which a caller reads with its own relations; a crossing of a boundary the source represents by no region; or an entry into the region, which has its own concept.", "definition": null, "args": [{"name": "u", "sort": "track"}, {"name": "r", "sort": "region"}], "params": [], "elements": [{"span": "it does not overlap the region at the observation and did overlap it at the observation before", "atoms": ["rel.occupies"], "concepts": [], "justification": "rel.occupies is 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (roadway, shoulder, sidewalk, intersection, crosswalk, stop line, safety zone, bicycle lane, median, alley, curb zone, controlled-access lane, structure)', which is the overlap the contract reads at the observation and at the one before; the region is the formal r the caller binds, so no region of the scene other than the one the caller singles out is read. Exclusion: the relation carries the footprint's overlap and not the geometry of the region (st.region_geometry), no distance being read, and not a direction or a speed of departure, which the contract expressly does not state."}], "residues": [], "literals": [], "scenarios": [{"name": "holds", "expected": "true", "narrative": "A vehicle's footprint overlaps an intersection region at one observation and, at the next, lies wholly clear of it: the concept holds at that next observation.", "masked": []}, {"name": "fails", "expected": "false", "narrative": "A vehicle's footprint overlaps the intersection region at both observations, having only moved farther into it: the concept fails. It fails as well at the observation after the departure, when the footprint lay clear of the region at the observation before.", "masked": []}, {"name": "blind", "expected": "unknown", "narrative": "The source does not observe which regions the vehicle's footprint overlaps, so whether the overlap with the region has just ended cannot be told.", "masked": ["rel.occupies"]}], "used_by": ["NRS_484B_400_2b"], "supersedes": null, "differs_from": {"concept": "drv.motion.region_entry", "why": "The sorts and the atom are the same as drv.motion.region_entry's, but the event is the opposite one: region_entry rises where the footprint comes to overlap the region, having not overlapped it at the observation before, while this concept rises where it ceases to overlap the region, having overlapped it at the observation before. Neither implies the other and no instantiation of one gives the other's verdict."}}

{"concept_id": "drv.motion.region_exit", "kind": "formula", "contract": "The road user's footprint ceases to overlap a structure region at the observation: it does not overlap the region at the observation and did overlap it at the observation before. Not a stand-in for: lying outside the region, which the occupancy relation carries on its own; a later observation at which the road user is still outside; the carrier or the way the road user goes on to, which a caller reads with its own relations; a crossing of a boundary the source represents by no region; or an entry into the region, which has its own concept.", "definition": null, "args": [{"name": "u", "sort": "track"}, {"name": "r", "sort": "region"}], "params": [], "elements": [{"span": "it does not overlap the region at the observation and did overlap it at the observation before", "atoms": ["rel.occupies"], "concepts": [], "justification": "rel.occupies is 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (roadway, shoulder, sidewalk, intersection, crosswalk, stop line, safety zone, bicycle lane, median, alley, curb zone, controlled-access lane, structure)', which is the overlap the contract reads at the observation and at the one before; the region is the formal r the caller binds, so no region of the scene other than the one the caller singles out is read. {"concept_id": "drv.motion.region_exit", "kind": "formula", "contract": "The road user's footprint ceases to overlap a structure region at the observation: it does not overlap the region at the observation and did overlap it at the observation before. The concept is the event of that ceasing to overlap, read at the observation at which the overlap has ended, and not the state of lying outside the region at the later observations. It states no direction of departure, no carrier the road user leaves through, no speed and no place outside the region. Not a stand-in for: lying outside the region, which the occupancy relation carries on its own; a later observation at which the road user is still outside; the carrier or the way the road user goes on to, which a caller reads with its own relations; a crossing of a boundary the source represents by no region; or an entry into the region, which has its own concept.", "definition": null, "args": [{"name": "u", "sort": "track"}, {"name": "r", "sort": "region"}], "params": [], "elements": [{"span": "it does not overlap the region at the observation and did overlap it at the observation before", "atoms": ["rel.occupies"], "concepts": [], "justification": "rel.occupies is 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (roadway, shoulder, sidewalk, intersection, crosswalk, stop line, safety zone, bicycle lane, median, alley, curb zone, controlled-access lane, structure)', which is the overlap the contract reads at the observation and at the one before; the region is the formal r the caller binds, so no region of the scene other than the one the caller singles out is read. Exclusion: the relation carries the footprint's overlap and not the geometry of the region (st.region_geometry), no distance being read, and not a direction or a speed of departure, which the contract expressly does not state."}], "residues": [], "literals": [], "scenarios": [{"name": "holds", "expected": "compliant", "narrative": "A vehicle's footprint overlaps an intersection region at one observation and, at the next, lies wholly clear of it: the concept holds at that next observation.", "masked": []}, {"name": "fails", "expected": "violated", "narrative": "A vehicle's footprint overlaps the intersection region at both observations, having only moved farther into it: the concept fails. It fails as well at the observation after the departure, when the footprint lay clear of the region at the observation before.", "masked": []}, {"name": "blind", "expected": "unknown", "narrative": "The source does not observe which regions the vehicle's footprint overlaps, so whether the overlap with the region has just ended cannot be told.", "masked": ["rel.occupies"]}], "used_by": ["NRS_484B_400_2b"], "supersedes": null, "differs_from": {"concept": "drv.motion.region_entry", "why": "The sorts and the atom are the same as drv.motion.region_entry's, but the event is the opposite one: region_entry rises where the footprint comes to overlap the region, having not overlapped it at the observation before, while this concept rises where it ceases to overlap the region, having overlapped it at the observation before. lines: {"node_id": "NRS_484B_400_2b", "law_refs": ["NRS-484B-400-2b"], "subject": {"binder": "v", "class_elements": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]}, "segmentation": [{"id": "s1", "text": "If the driver of a vehicle", "role": "subject"}, {"id": "s2", "text": "intends to turn", "role": "condition"}, {"id": "s3", "text": "at an intersection and:", "role": "condition"}, {"id": "s4", "text": "Both intersecting highways are two-directional:", "role": "condition"}, {"id": "s5", "text": "After entering the intersection,", "role": "condition"}, {"id": "s6", "text": "the left turn", "role": "condition"}, {"id": "s7", "text": "must be made so as to leave the intersection to the right of the centerline of the highway being entered.", "role": "obligation"}], "elements": [{"span": "s1", "atoms": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"], "derived": [], "justification": "'vehicle' is a legal aggregate and the definitions table admits DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle for this law; ru.aggregate carries 'membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id', so the words are claimed as the one atom with that id. Exclusions: not a stand-in for a named road-user class, since no class atom is used and the aggregate stays one atom; not a stand-in for a relational role such as who drives or controls a vehicle, so 'the driver' is not carried by the aggregate but read through the vehicle's controlled motion (narrowing on this span)."}, {"span": "s3", "atoms": ["rel.occupies", "st.intersection", "st.lane_enters", "st.travel_region"], "derived": [], "justification": "Reuse of the mapping index for these same words in NRS_484B_400_2a. st.intersection is 'the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges', the junction the words name; rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region', anchors the vehicle to the carrier it is on, and st.lane_enters gives 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end', so the intersection the words single out is the one the carrier the vehicle occupies enters; st.travel_region, 'the union of the kinds a device can govern: a lane and the kinds that refine it ... a roadway ... or an intersection', is the kind the carrier quantifier ranges over. Exclusions: st.intersection is not a stand-in for a crosswalk or a stop line, neither of which is read; st.lane_enters is not a stand-in for lane connectivity or for the subject's presence in the intersection, which rel.occupies carries; st.travel_region is not a stand-in for the extent of a highway, read by its own atom on s4."}, {"span": "s4", "atoms": ["rel.occupies", "st.highway", "st.intersection", "st.lane_direction", "st.lane_enters", "st.median_or_divider", "st.on_way", "st.roadway", "st.travel_region"], "derived": [], "justification": "Reuse of the mapping index for these same words in NRS_484B_400_2a. DEF-NRS-484B-073 defines a two-directional highway as 'an undivided highway upon which vehicles are allowed to proceed in opposite directions': st.median_or_divider, 'physical barrier or dividing section between roadways', carries 'undivided' by the absence of such a region on the way, and st.lane_direction, 'direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in ... a roadway, one-way roadway or shoulder', carries 'proceed in opposite directions' by two carriers of the same way carrying opposed designated directions. The two ways are reached through the junction: st.lane_enters names the carriers whose entrance end is that intersection, st.travel_region is the kind they are quantified by, st.roadway 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic' is the kind whose directions are designated, st.on_way 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on' and st.highway 'the entire public way between its boundary lines' give the highway each carrier lies on, st.intersection the junction itself, and rel.occupies anchors the subject. Exclusions: st.median_or_divider is read for the physical barrier its contract denotes and not for a legal designation of a highway, which would be an assumption; st.lane_direction is local to its carrier, which is why it is read on the carriers of each intersecting way and not at a point; st.roadway is not a stand-in for the sidewalk, which is not read."}, {"span": "s5", "atoms": ["rel.occupies", "st.intersection"], "derived": ["drv.motion.region_entry"], "justification": "drv.motion.region_entry is 'the road user's footprint comes to overlap a structure region at the observation: it overlaps the region at the observation and did not overlap it at the observation before ... the event of that coming to overlap', which is 'entering the intersection'; the region formal is bound to the intersection s3 singles out, so the entry is into that junction and not into any region of its kind. rel.occupies anchors the vehicle on the region and st.intersection is the kind the region quantifier names. The mapping index maps 'prior to entering an intersection' to the same carriers. Exclusions: the concept is not a stand-in for lying within the region afterwards, which rel.occupies carries on its own, nor for the carrier the road user came through."}, {"span": "s6", "atoms": [], "derived": ["drv.motion.left_turn"], "justification": "drv.motion.left_turn is 'the road user has turned to the left: counting from the onset of the turning ... the heading change accumulated since that onset reaches at least the turn angle ... to the left', which is 'the left turn' the words name, the manoeuvre whose manner the obligation governs. Exclusions: the concept is not a stand-in for a signal or a declared intention (the intention of s2 is carried by int.turn), not for a steering input, not for the curvature of the road, not for a lane change, and not for a reversal of the direction of travel, which is a larger angle with its own concept."}, {"span": "s7", "atoms": ["prim.region_lateral_offset", "rel.occupies", "st.centre_line", "st.highway", "st.intersection", "st.on_way"], "derived": ["drv.motion.region_exit"], "justification": "'leave the intersection' is drv.motion.region_exit, 'the road user's footprint ceases to overlap a structure region at the observation: it does not overlap the region at the observation and did overlap it at the observation before ... the event of that ceasing to overlap', with its region formal bound to the intersection s3 singles out, so the departure is from that junction; rel.occupies anchors the vehicle and st.intersection is the kind that region quantifier names. 'the centerline of the highway being entered' is a st.centre_line region, 'the marking, or the geometric centre, dividing the two directions of a two-way roadway', tied to the way by st.on_way, 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on', on the st.highway region, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines', that the vehicle occupies at that observation (rel.occupies). 'to the right of' is prim.region_lateral_offset, 'the signed lateral offset (m, left positive) of a structure region from a road user ... the component, perpendicular to the road user's heading, of the vector from its reference point to the point of the region's boundary nearest that reference point': the centre line lies to the vehicle's left, so the vehicle lies to its right. Exclusions: prim.region_lateral_offset 'does not establish that the road user is on the carrier', which rel.occupies does; st.centre_line is the dividing marking or geometric centre and no lane or lane adjacency stands in for it; st.highway is not a stand-in for the roadway, and the words name the highway being entered."}], "operationalizations": [], "assumptions": [], "intentions": [{"span": "s2", "id": "int.turn", "meaning": "the source's current plan for the road user is that it turn, to either hand, at the region named as the declaration's target"}], "compositions": [], "residues": [], "binders": [{"name": "v", "class_elements": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]}], "applicability": "The subject vehicle v occupies a carrier whose entrance end is an intersection i (st.lane_enters, the carrier quantified over st.travel_region, rel.occupies); the source's current declaration for v at i is int.turn; both highways that meet at i are two-directional, each way carrying no median or dividing section (st.median_or_divider absent on it) and carriers of its roadway carrying opposed designated directions (st.lane_direction), the ways reached by st.on_way and st.highway from the carriers that enter i; v has entered i (drv.motion.region_entry on i at the judged observation or at an earlier one); and v has made a left turn (drv.motion.left_turn, with p.turn_onset_yaw_rate, p.left_turn_angle and the step bound p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph).", "obligation": "At the observation at which v leaves i (drv.motion.region_exit on the intersection i the applicability binds), v lies to the right of the centre line of the highway it then occupies: for the st.highway region h with rel.occupies(v, h) at that observation there is a st.centre_line region c with st.on_way(c, h) whose signed lateral offset from v, prim.region_lateral_offset (left positive), is at least p.lateral_offset_resolution. Where no such centre line is observed on that way the obligation is unknown, not met.", "params": ["p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph", "p.turn_onset_yaw_rate", "p.left_turn_angle", "p.lateral_offset_resolution"], "narrowings": [{"span": "s1", "why": "'the driver of a vehicle' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the ontology's section on what is not an atom directs that 'drives', 'operates' and 'the driver' are read through the vehicle's controlled motion, a vehicle moving on the road is taken to be driven, and the duty binds that vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.", "kind": "observable_reading", "category": "agency"}, {"span": "s7", "why": "'the highway being entered' is read as the st.highway region the vehicle occupies at the observation at which it leaves the intersection, and 'the centerline' of it as a centre-line region lying on that way (st.on_way). {"concept_id": "drv.motion.region_exit", "kind": "formula", "contract": "The road user's footprint ceases to overlap a structure region at the observation: it does not overlap the region at the observation and did overlap it at the observation before. The concept is the event of that ceasing to overlap, read at the observation at which the overlap has ended, and not the state of lying outside the region at the later observations. It states no direction of departure, no carrier the road user leaves through, no speed and no place outside the region. Not a stand-in for: lying outside the region, which the occupancy relation carries on its own; a later observation at which the road user is still outside; the carrier or the way the road user goes on to, which a caller reads with its own relations; a crossing of a boundary the source represents by no region; or an entry into the region, which has its own concept.", "definition": null, "args": [{"name": "u", "sort": "track"}, {"name": "r", "sort": "region"}], "params": [], "elements": [{"span": "it does not overlap the region at the observation and did overlap it at the observation before", "atoms": ["rel.occupies"], "concepts": [], "justification": "rel.occupies is 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (roadway, shoulder, sidewalk, intersection, crosswalk, stop line, safety zone, bicycle lane, median, alley, curb zone, controlled-access lane, structure)', which is the overlap the contract reads at the observation and at the one before; the region is the formal r the caller binds, so no region of the scene other than the one the caller singles out is read. Exclusion: the relation carries the footprint's overlap and not the geometry of the region (st.region_geometry), no distance being read, and not a direction or a speed of departure, which the contract expressly does not state."}], "residues": [], "literals": [], "scenarios": [{"name": "holds", "expected": "compliant", "narrative": "A vehicle's footprint overlaps an intersection region at one observation and, at the next, lies wholly clear of it: the concept holds at that next observation.", "masked": []}, {"name": "fails", "expected": "violated", "narrative": "A vehicle's footprint overlaps the intersection region at both observations, having only moved farther into it: the concept fails. It fails as well at the observation after the departure, when the footprint lay clear of the region at the observation before.", "masked": []}, {"name": "blind", "expected": "unknown", "narrative": "The source does not observe which regions the vehicle's footprint overlaps, so whether the overlap with the region has just ended cannot be told.", "masked": ["rel.occupies"]}], "used_by": ["NRS_484B_400_2b"], "supersedes": null, "differs_from": {"concept": "drv.motion.region_entry", "why": "The sorts and the atom are the same as drv.motion.region_entry's, but the event is the opposite one: region_entry rises where the footprint comes to overlap the region, having not overlapped it at the observation before, while this concept rises where it ceases to overlap the region, having overlapped it at the observation before. Neither implies the other and no instantiation of one gives the other's verdict."}}

lines: {"node_id": "NRS_484B_400_2b", "law_refs": ["NRS-484B-400-2b"], "subject": {"binder": "v", "class_elements": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]}, "segmentation": [{"id": "s1", "text": "If the driver of a vehicle", "role": "subject"}, {"id": "s2", "text": "intends to turn", "role": "condition"}, {"id": "s3", "text": "at an intersection and:", "role": "condition"}, {"id": "s4", "text": "Both intersecting highways are two-directional:", "role": "condition"}, {"id": "s5", "text": "After entering the intersection,", "role": "condition"}, {"id": "s6", "text": "the left turn", "role": "condition"}, {"id": "s7", "text": "must be made so as to leave the intersection to the right of the centerline of the highway being entered.", "role": "obligation"}], "elements": [{"span": "s1", "atoms": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"], "derived": [], "justification": "'vehicle' is a legal aggregate and the definitions table admits DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle for this law; ru.aggregate carries 'membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id', so the words are claimed as the one atom with that id. The mapping index maps these same words in NRS_484B_400_2a to this atom and they mean the same here. Exclusions: not a stand-in for a named road-user class, since no class atom is used and the aggregate stays one atom; not a stand-in for a relational role such as who drives or controls a vehicle, so 'the driver' is not carried by the aggregate but read through the vehicle's controlled motion (narrowing on this span)."}, {"span": "s3", "atoms": ["rel.occupies", "st.intersection", "st.lane_enters", "st.travel_region"], "derived": [], "justification": "Reuse of the mapping index for these same words in NRS_484B_400_2a. st.intersection is 'the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges', the junction the words name; rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region', anchors the vehicle to the carrier it is on, and st.lane_enters gives 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end', so the intersection the words single out is the one the carrier the vehicle occupies enters; st.travel_region, 'the union of the kinds a device can govern: a lane and the kinds that refine it ... a roadway ... or an intersection', is the kind the carrier quantifier ranges over. Exclusions: st.intersection is not a stand-in for a crosswalk or a stop line, neither of which is read; st.lane_enters is not a stand-in for lane connectivity or for the subject's presence in the intersection, which rel.occupies carries; st.travel_region is not a stand-in for the extent of a highway, read by its own atom on s4."}, {"span": "s4", "atoms": ["rel.occupies", "st.highway", "st.intersection", "st.lane_direction", "st.lane_enters", "st.median_or_divider", "st.on_way", "st.roadway", "st.travel_region"], "derived": [], "justification": "Reuse of the mapping index for these same words in NRS_484B_400_2a. DEF-NRS-484B-073 defines a two-directional highway as 'an undivided highway upon which vehicles are allowed to proceed in opposite directions': st.median_or_divider, 'physical barrier or dividing section between roadways', carries 'undivided' by the absence of such a region on the way, and st.lane_direction, 'direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in ... a roadway, one-way roadway or shoulder', carries 'proceed in opposite directions' by two carriers of the same way carrying opposed designated directions. The two ways are reached through the junction: st.lane_enters names the carriers whose entrance end is that intersection, st.travel_region is the kind they are quantified by, st.roadway 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic' is the kind whose directions are designated, st.on_way 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on' and st.highway 'the entire public way between its boundary lines' give the highway each carrier lies on, st.intersection the junction itself, and rel.occupies anchors the subject. Exclusions: st.median_or_divider is read for the physical barrier its contract denotes and not for a legal designation of a highway, which would be an assumption; st.lane_direction is local to its carrier, which is why it is read on the carriers of each intersecting way and not at a point; st.roadway is not a stand-in for the sidewalk, which is not read."}, {"span": "s5", "atoms": ["rel.occupies", "st.intersection"], "derived": ["drv.motion.region_entry"], "justification": "drv.motion.region_entry is 'the road user's footprint comes to overlap a structure region at the observation: it overlaps the region at the observation and did not overlap it at the observation before ... the event of that coming to overlap', which is 'entering the intersection'; the region formal is bound to the intersection s3 singles out, so the entry is into that junction and not into any region of its kind. rel.occupies anchors the vehicle on the region and st.intersection is the kind the region quantifier names. The mapping index maps 'prior to entering an intersection' to the same carriers. Exclusions: the concept is not a stand-in for lying within the region afterwards, which rel.occupies carries on its own, nor for the carrier the road user came through."}, {"span": "s6", "atoms": [], "derived": ["drv.motion.left_turn"], "justification": "drv.motion.left_turn is 'the road user has turned to the left: counting from the onset of the turning ... the heading change accumulated since that onset reaches at least the turn angle ... to the left', which is 'the left turn' the words name, the manoeuvre whose manner the obligation governs. Exclusions: the concept is not a stand-in for a signal or a declared intention (the intention of s2 is carried by int.turn), not for a steering input, not for the curvature of the road, not for a lane change, and not for a reversal of the direction of travel, which is a larger angle with its own concept."}, {"span": "s7", "atoms": ["prim.region_lateral_offset", "rel.occupies", "st.centre_line", "st.highway", "st.intersection", "st.on_way"], "derived": ["drv.motion.region_exit"], "justification": "'leave the intersection' is drv.motion.region_exit, 'the road user's footprint ceases to overlap a structure region at the observation: it does not overlap the region at the observation and did overlap it at the observation before ... the event of that ceasing to overlap', with its region formal bound to the intersection s3 singles out, so the departure is from that junction; rel.occupies anchors the vehicle and st.intersection is the kind that region quantifier names. 'the centerline of the highway being entered' is a st.centre_line region, 'the marking, or the geometric centre, dividing the two directions of a two-way roadway', tied to the way by st.on_way, 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on', on the st.highway region, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines', that the vehicle occupies at that observation (rel.occupies). 'to the right of' is prim.region_lateral_offset, 'the signed lateral offset (m, left positive) of a structure region from a road user ... the component, perpendicular to the road user's heading, of the vector from its reference point to the point of the region's boundary nearest that reference point': the centre line lies to the vehicle's left, so the vehicle lies to its right. Exclusions: prim.region_lateral_offset 'does not establish that the road user is on the carrier', which rel.occupies does; st.centre_line is the dividing marking or geometric centre and no lane or lane adjacency stands in for it; st.highway is not a stand-in for the roadway, and the words name the highway being entered."}], "operationalizations": [], "assumptions": [], "intentions": [{"span": "s2", "id": "int.turn", "meaning": "the source's current plan for the road user is that it turn, to either hand, at the region named as the declaration's target"}], "compositions": [], "residues": [], "binders": [{"name": "v", "class_elements": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]}], "applicability": "The subject vehicle v occupies a carrier whose entrance end is an intersection i (st.lane_enters, the carrier quantified over st.travel_region, rel.occupies); the source's current declaration for v at i is int.turn; both highways that meet at i are two-directional, each way carrying no median or dividing section (st.median_or_divider absent on it) and carriers of its roadway carrying opposed designated directions (st.lane_direction), the ways reached by st.on_way and st.highway from the carriers that enter i; v has entered i (drv.motion.region_entry on i at the judged observation or at an earlier one); and v has made a left turn (drv.motion.left_turn, with p.turn_onset_yaw_rate, p.left_turn_angle and the step bound p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph).", "obligation": "At the observation at which v leaves i (drv.motion.region_exit on the intersection i the applicability binds), v lies to the right of the centre line of the highway it then occupies: for the st.highway region h with rel.occupies(v, h) at that observation there is a st.centre_line region c with st.on_way(c, h) whose signed lateral offset from v, prim.region_lateral_offset (left positive), is at least p.lateral_offset_resolution. Where no such centre line is observed on that way the obligation is unknown, not met.", "params": ["p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph", "p.turn_onset_yaw_rate", "p.left_turn_angle", "p.lateral_offset_resolution"], "narrowings": [{"span": "s1", "why": "'the driver of a vehicle' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the ontology's section on what is not an atom directs that 'drives', 'operates' and 'the driver' are read through the vehicle's controlled motion, a vehicle moving on the road is taken to be driven, and the duty binds that vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.", "kind": "observable_reading", "category": "agency"}, {"span": "s7", "why": "'the highway being entered' is read as the st.highway region the vehicle occupies at the observation at which it leaves the intersection, and 'the centerline' of it as a centre-line region lying on that way (st.on_way). The words leave open which way is meant; this is the way the vehicle is on once it is clear of the junction, the junction itself lying on every way that meets there.", "kind": "reading"}, {"span": "s7", "why": "'to the right of the centerline' is read as the centre line's signed lateral offset from the vehicle standing at or above p.lateral_offset_resolution on the left-positive side, the magnitude below which the side a region lies on is not distinguishable at the source's resolution; the side is read across the vehicle's own heading, which at the departure from the junction lies along the way entered.", "kind": "reading"}], "scenarios": [{"name": "forbid", "expected": "violated", "narrative": "Two undivided ways, each with carriers of opposed designated directions, cross; the trace declares the subject's intention to turn at that junction; the subject enters the junction and its accumulated heading change to the left passes the turn angle, so a left turn is made. At the observation at which its footprint ceases to overlap the junction it is on the far side of the entered way's centre line, the centre line lying to its right.", "masked": []}, {"name": "permit", "expected": "compliant", "narrative": "The same two two-directional ways, the same declared intention, the same entry and left turn; at the observation at which the subject's footprint ceases to overlap the junction the centre line of the way it then occupies lies to its left by more than the lateral-offset resolution. No other road user is present in the scene.", "masked": []}, {"name": "idle", "expected": "not_applicable", "narrative": "The subject runs straight through the same junction: the trace declares no intention to turn for it at that junction and its accumulated heading change never reaches the turn angle, so no left turn is made.", "masked": []}, {"name": "blind", "expected": "unknown", "narrative": "Every other condition holds -- two two-directional ways, the declared intention, the entry, and a departure from the junction on the left of the entered way's centre line -- but the source supplies no rate of change of heading for the subject, so whether it has turned to the left cannot be told.", "masked": ["kin.yaw_rate"]}, {"name": "branch_1", "expected": "not_applicable", "narrative": "The way being entered carries a median dividing its two directions, so the intersecting ways are not both two-directional; the subject, with a declared intention to turn, enters the junction, turns left and leaves it on the left of that way's centre line.", "masked": []}], "literals": [], "param_proposals": [{"name": "p.lateral_offset_resolution", "unit": "m", "value": 0.5, "convention": "Lateral-offset convention: the magnitude of a signed lateral offset below which the side a region lies on is not distinguishable at the source's resolution, so that an offset smaller than it decides no side; it names the source's resolution only and sets no measure of how far from the line a vehicle must be.", "source": "the lateral accuracy of mapped region boundaries and of a body's reference point in a scene-graph source, of the order of half a metre."}, {"name": "p.left_turn_angle", "unit": "deg", "value": 45.0, "convention": "Turn-recognition convention: the heading change accumulated since the onset at which a turn to the left is recognized as made, taken as the angle at which a body has committed to a left turn at a junction rather than a lane change or a drift within its lane.", "source": "manoeuvre-recognition practice for junction turns, which treats an accumulated heading change of about a quarter turn as a committed turn."}, {"name": "p.turn_onset_yaw_rate", "unit": "deg/s", "value": 3.0, "convention": "Manoeuvre-onset convention: the rate of change of heading above which a body is read as turning rather than running straight, set at the noise floor of a yaw reading so that the onset of a manoeuvre is told from lane-keeping corrections.", "source": "yaw-rate noise of vehicle-dynamics and scene-graph sources at open-road speeds."}], "gaps": []}

-{"node_id": "NRS_484B_407", "law_refs": ["NRS-484B-407"], "subject": {"binder": "v", "class_elements": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]}, "segmentation": [{"id": "s1", "text": "A vehicle", "role": "subject"}, {"id": "s2", "text": "shall not be turned so as to proceed in the opposite direction", "role": "obligation"}, {"id": "s3", "text": "upon any curve,", "role": "condition"}, {"id": "s4", "text": "or upon the approach to or near the crest of a grade,", "role": "condition"}, {"id": "s5", "text": "where such vehicle cannot be seen by the driver of any other vehicle approaching from either direction within 500 feet.", "role": "condition"}], "elements": [{"span": "s1", "atoms": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"], "derived": [], "justification": "'vehicle' is a legal aggregate and the definitions table admits DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle for this law; ru.aggregate carries 'membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id'. {"concept_id": "drv.motion.region_exit", "kind": "formula", "contract": "The road user's footprint ceases to overlap a structure region at the observation: it does not overlap the region at the observation and did overlap it at the observation before. The concept is the event of that ceasing to overlap, read at the observation at which the overlap has ended, and not the state of lying outside the region at the later observations. It states no direction of departure, no carrier the road user leaves through, no speed and no place outside the region. Not a stand-in for: lying outside the region, which the occupancy relation carries on its own; a later observation at which the road user is still outside; the carrier or the way the road user goes on to, which a caller reads with its own relations; a crossing of a boundary the source represents by no region; or an entry into the region, which has its own concept.", "definition": null, "args": [{"name": "u", "sort": "track"}, {"name": "r", "sort": "region"}], "params": [], "elements": [{"span": "it does not overlap the region at the observation and did overlap it at the observation before", "atoms": ["rel.occupies"], "concepts": [], "justification": "rel.occupies is 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (roadway, shoulder, sidewalk, intersection, crosswalk, stop line, safety zone, bicycle lane, median, alley, curb zone, controlled-access lane, structure)', which is the overlap the contract reads at the observation and at the one before; the region is the formal r the caller binds, so no region of the scene other than the one the caller singles out is read. Exclusion: the relation carries the footprint's overlap and not the geometry of the region (st.region_geometry), no distance being read, and not a direction or a speed of departure, which the contract expressly does not state."}], "residues": [], "literals": [], "scenarios": [{"name": "holds", "expected": "compliant", "narrative": "A vehicle's footprint overlaps an intersection region at one observation and, at the next, lies wholly clear of it: the concept holds at that next observation.", "masked": []}, {"name": "fails", "expected": "violated", "narrative": "A vehicle's footprint overlaps the intersection region at both observations, having only moved farther into it: the concept fails. It fails as well at the observation after the departure, when the footprint lay clear of the region at the observation before.", "masked": []}, {"name": "blind", "expected": "unknown", "narrative": "The source does not observe which regions the vehicle's footprint overlaps, so whether the overlap with the region has just ended cannot be told.", "masked": ["rel.occupies"]}], "used_by": ["NRS_484B_400_2b"], "supersedes": null, "differs_from": {"concept": "drv.motion.region_entry", "why": "The sorts and the atom are the same as drv.motion.region_entry's, but the event is the opposite one: region_entry rises where the footprint comes to overlap the region, having not overlapped it at the observation before, while this concept rises where it ceases to overlap the region, having overlapped it at the observation before. Neither implies the other and no instantiation of one gives the other's verdict."}}
